target_customer: Indie music listeners (free, ad and affiliate supported) and independent artists
problem: Discovering good independent music among a flood of uploads was hard; recommendation relied on editors or algorithms.
business_model: Ad supported streaming with Amazon affiliate links; artists could sell downloads

founders.name: Samuel Hsiung
founders.background_notes: YC page and Wikipedia; Wikipedia says the site was created by two USC students per other coverage (search summary), not verified

founders.name: James Miao
founders.background_notes: Named as founder on Wikipedia, not on the YC page

exit.reason: Founders announced in April 2017 that thesixtyone would go offline on May 1, 2017 and promised a final payment to artists; no financial reason stated in the summary I saw

competitors.name: Hype Machine
competitors.what: Music blog aggregator that also uses hearts for voting

technical_complexity.rationale: Ajax navigation keeping audio playing across pages, voting and reputation systems and tag playlists in 2008 to 2009; moderate engineering by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Community reputation and badges created some stickiness, but the redesign in January 2010 drove away many of the most active users, showing the community moat was thin.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition occurred; the site ran until May 2017.

market_need_then: Indie music was growing and artists wanted exposure; TechCrunch in March 2009 reported Paul Graham calling the service ramen profitable from ads and Amazon affiliate links, showing early traction.

branding.name_origin: The thesixtyone site is named for Highway 61, a route tied to American music culture, per Wikipedia. The company name Recurious has no sourced origin.
branding.domain_note: Brand domain thesixtyone.com; origin not found
branding.community_and_virality: Active users who protested the January 2010 redesign and a founder apology in January 2016 reverting it, per Wikipedia and TechCrunch.

brand_strength.rationale: Consumer brand praised for design in a Next Web headline and had an engaged community with reputation levels and hearts, but it was niche and the 2010 redesign backlash showed users cared about its identity.

outcome_analysis: Thesixtyone grew as a community music discovery site and was near ramen profitable in 2009, then lost many of its most active users after a January 2010 redesign. It stayed online until May 2017 with little funding visible. Failure factors are inferences from the long decline and limited scale, since the founders gave no financial reason.
notes: The 2013 Series B of $1.5M from Greylock rests on a single database (CB Insights) seen only in a search summary; the page returned 403. It is internally inconsistent (listed active, Sunnyvale, three rounds but two investors) and may be a data error, so treat as unverified. Angel investors named by Wikipedia without amounts. Wikipedia and a search summary differ on founder details. Company website field in the directory is empty. Failure factors inferred.
